items.canonicalSource: .memory/wiki/specs/ideation/17-live-booking-settlement/17.02-offers-negotiation/17.02.01-offer-sheet-composition.md:61-72 (§ The Economic-Signal Lint, ratified at D-06 :235) — four number-anchored signal classes including "an economic noun/verb within 40 characters of a number", with the ≥95%-recall design target stated
items.summary: 17.03.01 D-09 decides only that economic content in free text is detected and must be acknowledged — it specifies no trigger conditions and no keywords. The trigger spec exists solely in 17.02.01's ratified lint section, and 17.03.01's own cross-cut already assigns the mechanism to that feature ("The economic-content detector (D-09) fires at that feature's send action"). The edge-case cell was therefore a compressed restatement that dropped the number-proximity qualifier from all four classes at once — drift, not a second design. Replaced the restated conditions and duplicate keyword list with a reference to 17.02.01 D-06, stating explicitly that a money keyword with no adjacent number does not fire, and clarified the ownership split in the cross-cut (which also carried a stale pointer to 17.02.01's renumbered Q-02). Did not touch the canonical list: the three keywords the local copy carried and 17.02.01 lacks (`less`, `owed`, `guarantee` — `guarantee` being this vocabulary's most load-bearing term) are recorded in a new Q-07 (Agent → /write-be-spec with 17.02.01) rather than dropped or silently merged into another file's ratified decision.
